acceptance: A wrapper option its table does not list, followed by a word that could be git once a trailing ')' is removed, is refused with the unlisted-option reason inside a ( ) subshell whose closing paren touches that word, exactly as the bare command is. Verified allowed on WIP 1b2fcbd1 (2026-11-20) and refused after this leaf: '(sudo -Q $X)', '( sudo -Q $X)', '(sudo -Q "$X")', '(sudo -Q ${X})', '(sudo -Q g$X)', '(env -Q $X)', '(nohup -x $X)', '(doas -Q $CMD)', '(nice -5 $X)', 'x=1; (sudo -Q $X)', '(sudo -Q $X); ls', '! (sudo -Q $X)' and '{ (sudo -Q $X); }'
The trailing-paren strip that _unwrap applies to each word is one helper used by both _unwrap and the could-be-git check behind the unlisted-option refusal; no second copy of the rule exists

No command allowed on WIP 1b2fcbd1 becomes refused except one in the class above: '(sudo -Q ls)', '(sudo -Q ls )', 'sudo --not-a-sudo-option ls /tmp' and the ordinary-commands table stay allowed. Accepted and stated in the CHANGELOG entry: a quoted or escaped literal ')' ending a could-be-git word after an unlisted option is now refused

tests/unit/test_tool_call_guard.py::test_unlisted_wrapper_option_is_opaque gains the refused commands of the first criterion as hidden rows and '(sudo -Q ls)' and '(sudo -Q ls )' as allowed rows; no test is added, removed or renamed
CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] extends the guard Security entry; no version heading is written
nodes.title: The tool-call guard keeps the unlisted-option refusal when a subshell's closing paren touches the next word
